experiment_contract.claim: Test whether explicit train-only user-item/author affinity count features improve personalized ranking beyond the fixed SO feature set.
experiment_contract.expected_observable: Feature dimension increases above the delegated baseline 25 and predictions differ from parent on every seed.
experiment_contract.falsification_condition: No feature-dimension increase, or no measurable improvement/complementarity on validation.
forbidden_shortcuts: using validation/test labels or post-exposure targets as features
editing train to silently alter LightGBM fixed parameters
required_components: features block must append new columns derived from train-only user-author/user-video/user-tab counts
only inference-time IDs user_id/video_id/author_id/tab may index those aggregates
all splits must receive the same appended feature schema

fallback: If sparse pair counts are too zero-heavy, next step would back off to user-author and user-tab only rather than abandoning pair-personalization entirely.
hypothesis: Adding explicit train-only pair affinity features for (user,author), (user,video), and (user,tab) will improve within-user ranking and diversify errors relative to the current item/context ranker, which lacks direct pair-personalization features in its fixed 25-column representation.
implementation_plan: Edit features as primary and predict as support. In build_features, after calling SO.build_features(splits, train_idx, OP_CONFIG), load DV.load('train') and compute train-only count dictionaries for user-author, user-video, and user-tab interactions over the training rows referenced by train_idx. For each split, append dense float32 columns: log1p(user_author_count), log1p(user_video_count), log1p(user_tab_count), and normalized user_author_share = user_author_count / max(1,user_total_count). Counts use only train data; unseen pairs map to zero. In predict, keep SO.predict unchanged because the model consumes the expanded matrices directly.
justification: Counts over observed user-author and user-video histories are legal inference-time features because they are train-only aggregates over IDs available at inference. They directly target the pair-personalization requirement and can help cold-to-mid popularity slices where generic item/context scores underfit user-specific preferences.
observation: The task explicitly states that "personalization must depend on a (user, candidate-item) pair," while the trusted runtime says SO.build_features returns "25 fixed context/group-statistic columns" and the parent is named "Item/context LambdaRank," suggesting limited direct user-item interaction representation. Also the last directional feedback showed broad losses across all "train_item_popularity_quartile" slices, especially q1 delta -0.10655939890604793, consistent with weak memorization for rarer items.
research_nonuse_reason: The supplied research records do not directly cover adding train-only user-author/video affinity counts to the delegated LightGBM ranker; task constraints and current-code gaps are the more direct basis.
